key_insight: An equivalent-circuit model shows that the S-shaped voltage response and photoluminescence behavior of the valley photovoltaic device are caused by a reverse diode that impedes electron extraction.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies a concrete device-level failure mode in valley photovoltaics, giving designers a clear target for improving carrier extraction and pushing efficiency higher.
method: Collected electrical current-voltage characteristics showing S-shaped behavior.
Fit both optical and electrical data with a unified equivalent-circuit model, supported by Poisson/drift-diffusion analysis.
evidence_signal: The model simultaneously explains the device’s photoluminescence and electrical measurements, including the previously observed S-shaped current-voltage curves.
watch_item: The reverse-diode effect must be eliminated, and it may arise from either valley-scattering physics or a heterojunction barrier.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
